description: Controlled rayPath-to-viewSamples fixtures for sampleViewPath. These rows test midpoint sample placement, weights, metadata, empty-path handling, and direct-stage invalid packet rejection only.

expectedComparisonPolicy.nonnumeric: Exact structural comparison for object, array, string, boolean, and null expected values. Numeric sample distances and weights use each datum's tolerance rule.

reference.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
reference.derivationSummary: For empty ray paths, sampleViewPath returns an empty sample array and records midpoint metadata without inventing integration distance.

supportingReferences.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
supportingReferences.locator: Section 11.2, transmittance over a finite segment and zero-distance semantics.
supportingReferences.supports: No path distance means no path integral samples are needed.

assumptions.stageScope: rayPath is already resolved; no geometry or medium evaluation occurs here

viewSamples.units: km for sample distances and weights
viewSamples.derivation: Local sampleViewPath contract: isEmpty true and lengthKm 0 produce no samples.

viewSampleMetadata.derivation: Local sampleViewPath metadata contract records the fixed midpoint method, zero emitted samples, and zero path length.

expectations.independence: The expected output is pinned fixture data from the local packet contract, not generated by sampleViewPath.

reference.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
reference.locator: sampleViewPath Output Shape and resolveRayPath Boundary Precedence.
reference.derivationSummary: Zero-length boundary paths do not invent epsilon distance or zero-weight placeholder samples.

supportingReferences.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
supportingReferences.locator: Section 11.2, transmittance from a point to itself.
supportingReferences.supports: Zero-distance transport is meaningful and should not require artificial sample distance.

viewSamples.units: km for sample distances and weights
viewSamples.derivation: Local sampleViewPath contract: lengthKm 0 produces no integration samples.

viewSampleMetadata.derivation: Local sampleViewPath metadata contract records zero emitted samples and zero path length.

expectations.independence: The expected output is pinned fixture data for a zero-length packet boundary case.

reference.title: Numerical Integration, Midpoint Rule
reference.locator: Quadrature rules based on step functions; midpoint/rectangle rule formula.
reference.derivationSummary: The midpoint rule evaluates the interval at (a + b) / 2 and weights by interval width b - a.

supportingReferences.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
supportingReferences.supports: Packet field names and fixed midpoint method metadata.

viewSamples.units: km for sample distances and weights
viewSamples.derivation: Midpoint rule on [0, 10]: center = (0 + 10) / 2 = 5 km and weight = 10 - 0 = 10 km.

viewSampleMetadata.derivation: Local metadata contract records method midpoint, one emitted sample, and path length 10 km.

expectations.independence: Expected sample center and weight are hand-derived from midpoint-rule arithmetic.

expectations.quantity: two midpoint samples from zero-start segment

reference.title: Numerical Integration, Midpoint Rule
reference.locator: Quadrature rules based on step functions; midpoint/rectangle rule and composite subdivision.
reference.derivationSummary: Composite midpoint sampling partitions the interval into equal subintervals and evaluates each subinterval at its center.

supportingReferences.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
supportingReferences.supports: Packet field names and fixed midpoint method metadata.

viewSamples.units: km for sample distances and weights
viewSamples.derivation: Composite midpoint on [0, 10] with two equal subintervals: width = 10 / 2 = 5 km; centers are 0 + 2.5 = 2.5 km and 5 + 2.5 = 7.5 km.

viewSampleMetadata.derivation: Local metadata contract records method midpoint, two emitted samples, and path length 10 km.

expectations.independence: Expected samples are hand-derived from composite midpoint arithmetic.

expectations.quantity: two midpoint samples from nonzero-start segment

reference.title: Numerical Integration, Midpoint Rule
reference.locator: Quadrature rules based on step functions; midpoint/rectangle rule and composite subdivision.
reference.derivationSummary: Composite midpoint sampling applies the same center-and-width rule on a shifted interval.

supportingReferences.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
supportingReferences.supports: Distances remain measured from the observer along the selected camera ray.

viewSamples.units: km for sample distances and weights
viewSamples.derivation: Composite midpoint on [2, 12] with two equal subintervals: width = 10 / 2 = 5 km; centers are (2 + 7) / 2 = 4.5 km and (7 + 12) / 2 = 9.5 km.

viewSampleMetadata.derivation: Local metadata contract records method midpoint, two emitted samples, and path length 10 km.

expectations.independence: Expected samples are hand-derived from composite midpoint arithmetic on a shifted interval.

reference.title: Numerical Integration, Midpoint Rule
reference.locator: Numerical integration as weighted sums over subintervals.
reference.derivationSummary: Composite midpoint weights are subinterval widths, and the widths partition the full interval.

supportingReferences.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
supportingReferences.locator: Optical depth as path integral over distance ds.
supportingReferences.supports: sampleViewPath weights are later consumed as distance elements ds.

weightSumKm.derivation: Composite midpoint on [0, 10] with four equal subintervals has width 2.5 km each; 4 * 2.5 = 10 km.

expectations.independence: Expected total weight is pinned arithmetic from fixture-owned path length and viewSteps.

supportingReferences.title: Numerical Integration, Midpoint Rule
supportingReferences.locator: Composite midpoint subdivision over ordered subintervals.

distanceFromObserverKm.derivation: Composite midpoint on [0, 10] with four equal subintervals has width 2.5 km; centers are 1.25, 3.75, 6.25, and 8.75 km in increasing ray order.

expectations.independence: Expected ordered distances are pinned fixture data, not computed by sampleViewPath.

reference.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
reference.locator: sampleViewPath Output Shape and Error Handling.
reference.derivationSummary: sampleViewPath consumes ordered finite path distances. Negative length cannot define a forward integration measure.

supportingReferences.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
supportingReferences.locator: Optical depth as integral over finite distance.
supportingReferences.supports: Negative path length cannot be consumed as ds.

expectations.independence: The expected error follows from explicit invalid fixture data.

reference.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design
reference.locator: sampleViewPath Output Shape and packet validation.
reference.derivationSummary: The selected segment's length must match endKm - startKm so sample weights partition the same path later consumed by optical-depth integration.

supportingReferences.title: PBRT v4, Geometry and Transformations / Rays
supportingReferences.supports: Segment endpoints define the ordered path interval.

expectedError.derivation: Local direct-stage validation: endKm - startKm = 10 km but lengthKm = 9 km, so the segment data is contradictory.

expectations.independence: The expected error follows from explicit inconsistent fixture data.

reference.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design

supportingReferences.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance

expectations.independence: The expected errors follow from encoded invalid distance values.

reference.title: CPU Spectral Reference Code Design

reference.derivationSummary: viewSteps partitions the selected path into discrete samples, so direct stage packets require a positive finite integer when the control is present.

supportingReferences.supports: A sample count is a discrete partition count.
